newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open mixed, accounts stay sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open mixed, accounts stay sidelined.

text.p: Canadian T-bills open mixed in very quiet trade on Monday, with many accounts absent from the market amid speculation the Bank of Canada could soon hike rates, dealers said.

"The account side of things is pretty quiet so far. The bulk of the business we expect to see on Thursday again with the bill maturities but they continue to remain relatively short in anticipation of some move by the Bank of Canada," said one T-bill dealer with a Canadian bank.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded unchanged from Monday's close to yield 3.17 percent.

Speculation of a near-term Bank of Canada rate hike is being prompted by weakness in the Canadian dollar. The currency opened weaker at C$1.3951 (US$0.7167) on Tuesday. Analysts said markets have been driving the dollar gradually weaker to test the Bank of Canada's resolve to hold interest rates steady.
Rate hike speculation and a squeeze taking place with some when-issued T-bills are the primary factors affecting the money market this morning, the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.69 percent from 3.67 percent on Monday. The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 4.01 percent from 4.05 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.25 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
